questions.q: In which year was the Partition of Bengal announced by Lord Curzon, and what were the two new provinces created?
questions.a: The Partition was announced in 1905, creating Eastern Bengal and Assam (capital Dhaka) and Western Bengal (capital Calcutta). A wrong answer (e.g., 1911 or 1909) reveals the student confuses the Partition with its annulment or the Morley-Minto Reforms, showing they have not anchored the key date that triggers the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q: Why did nationalist leaders like Surendranath Banerjee and Rabindranath Tagore call the Partition a "divide and rule" policy rather than accepting the British claim of administrative convenience?
questions.a: The Partition separated Bengali-speaking Muslims in the east from Bengali-speaking Hindus in the west, deliberately cutting across linguistic and cultural unity to create a Muslim-majority province; the British ignored similar-sized provinces like Madras that were not divided. A wrong answer that accepts "administrative efficiency" shows the student misses the political motive and cannot see how colonial policies exploited religious differences—a pattern recurring in 1947.

questions.q: A student finds a 1906 newspaper advertisement: "Swadeshi Cotton Mills, Bombay—Buy Indian cloth, save the nation." Using your knowledge of the Swadeshi Movement, explain what economic and political message this advertisement carries.
questions.a: The advertisement reflects the Swadeshi strategy of linking economic self-reliance (buying Indian-made cloth instead of Manchester imports) to political nationalism ("save the nation"), turning everyday consumption into a patriotic act. A wrong answer that treats it as just a commercial ad misses the core innovation of Swadeshi: making economics a battlefield of nationalism, which Gandhi later expanded in Khadi.

questions.q: Compare the methods of the Moderates (petitions, prayers) and the Extremists (boycott, passive resistance) during the Swadeshi period. Why did this difference lead to the Surat Split of 1907?
questions.a: Moderates wanted to pressure the British through constitutional means within the empire; Extremists like Tilak and Lajpat Rai saw Swadeshi as a tool for self-rule (Swaraj) and advocated mass boycott and non-cooperation. The split occurred because Moderates feared loss of control and British repression, while Extremists demanded the Congress adopt the new militant methods. A wrong answer that calls it a "personality clash" misses the strategic disagreement about how to achieve independence.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "The Swadeshi Movement failed because the Partition was annulled in 1911." Provide two pieces of evidence to support your judgment.
questions.a: The statement is flawed: the Movement succeeded in forcing the 1911 annulment (evidence 1) and, more importantly, permanently changed Indian nationalism by introducing mass mobilization, indigenous enterprise (Bengal Chemicals, Tata Steel), and cultural renaissance (Tagore's songs, Bengal School of Art)—evidence 2. A wrong answer that judges only by the immediate outcome shows the student cannot assess long-term historical significance beyond surface events.

questions.q: Create a timeline with four key events showing how the Partition of Bengal (1905) connects to the rise of revolutionary nationalism (Anushilan Samiti) and the eventual Lucknow Pact (1916). Briefly explain each link.
questions.a: 1905 Partition → 1905–08 Swadeshi mass protests → 1907 Surat Split (Extremists leave Congress) → 1908–1910 Revolutionary turn (Anushilan Samiti bombings) → 1911 Annulment + capital shift to Delhi → 1913–16 Congress-League rapprochement (Lucknow Pact). A poor answer lists dates without showing causation—e.g., how Extremist exit pushed youth toward revolution, or how annulment created space for Hindu-Muslim unity talks.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Partition of Bengal (1905) was a British administrative decision by Viceroy Lord Curzon to divide the Bengal ______ into two provinces—Eastern Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) and Western Bengal (Hindu-majority)—ostensibly for administrative efficiency but widely seen as a "divide and rule" strategy.

Fill in the blank: Imagine you walk into a Kolkata market today and see a sign saying "Buy Indian"—that idea started in 1905 when ______ officials drew a line through Bengal to weaken Hindu-Muslim unity.

Fill in the blank: The Partition of Bengal (______) was a British administrative decision by Viceroy Lord Curzon to divide the Bengal Presidency into two provinces—Eastern Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) and Western Bengal (Hindu-majority)—ostensibly for administrative efficiency but widely seen as a "divide and rule" strategy.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can explain how the Partition of Bengal was a deliberate political strategy rather than an administrative necessity, and can analyze how the Swadeshi Movement transformed Indian nationalism from elite petitioning to mass mobilization with economic, cultural, and political dimensions.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you walk into a Kolkata market today and see a sign saying "Buy Indian"—that idea started in 1905 when British ______ drew a line through Bengal to weaken Hindu-Muslim unity.
